decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm's coolant-management offering, it likely has low carrying cost and still retains option value while market adoption unfolds.
The centrifuge fits the established filtration and coolant domain, so despite some commercialization uncertainty its strategic fit and learning value favor keeping it on the market.
Coolant nozzles are a low-cost complementary line with several models, making the option cheap to hold and useful for cross-selling into the existing installed base.
This conveyor is close rather than fully embedded in the established offer, so uncertainty is somewhat higher, but the growing industry and adjacency still support retaining it for now.
A magnetic belt chip conveyor builds directly on the firm's known material-handling capabilities, so management would likely continue offering it while demand evidence accumulates.
The hinged belt chip conveyor is an adjacent product with some uncertainty, but for a large engineering firm its portfolio role and moderate carrying cost make keeping it the more likely choice.
